_: THE CATALOGUE. Each pattern is an instructional situation with named slots and a small set of APPROVED SUBDESIGNS. A subdesign is selected by the SURFACE and — only where a pattern declares `aspects` — the media's own aspect class. There is no third input, and no rule anywhere may consult content. `areas` is grid-template-areas verbatim: the CSS is generated from this file, so the design and the layout cannot drift apart the way a grammar in prose once drifted from thresholds in a script. REVISED after a cross-pattern consistency review: `notes.basic` and `notes.examples-tabs` merged into `notes` (they differed by one slot, and the second was keyed on a DISCLOSURE MODE, which is an author axis decided inside a slot — a pattern keyed on an author axis is not a pattern); `practice.graph-workbook` folded into `practice.workbook` (identical slots plus `reference`; grid paper versus lined paper is a property of the handwrittenResponse BLOCK, and a pattern that forks on a block property has collapsed the two vocabularies); `interactive.primary`'s `workspace` renamed `instrument`, because one slot NAME was carrying two different slot TYPES; and `worked.single` added, because the catalogue could not lay out two of its own lesson's four subtopics.

notes.intent: Teaching notes: an explanation, optionally a rule set apart, optionally a set of equivalent worked examples. The default page of a lesson.

slots.name: intro
slots.rationale: What this page is about, before any detail.

slots.name: support
slots.rationale: A rule stated once and set apart. Beside the intro on desktop, where the two are read together; four columns, so it reads as subordinate without breaking the measure.

slots.name: reading
slots.rationale: The explanation itself, where the page has one. A table of values belongs to the explanation rather than to a track of its own.

slots.name: examples
slots.rationale: Equivalent sibling examples — the same move on different numbers. WHETHER THEY ARE SHOWN TOGETHER OR BEHIND TABS IS AUTHORED INSIDE THIS SLOT and is not what makes a pattern: the previous catalogue had a whole second pattern whose only distinguishing feature was the tabstrip.

slots.name: synthesis
slots.rationale: What the page adds up to.

slots.name: scenario
slots.rationale: The situation a modelling question sits inside — the bridge, the stone, the rule that came from somewhere. Present it BESIDE the solution on desktop so the reader can look back at the situation while following the algebra; absent, and the page is a plain worked example.

slots.name: worked
slots.rationale: The solution itself. THE ONLY REQUIRED SLOT: without it there is no worked example.

slots.name: support
slots.rationale: The move the example instances, stated once so it survives the arithmetic.

slots.name: synthesis
slots.rationale: What this one example establishes.

visual.explanation.intent: One primary visual and the reading of it, where the READING carries the teaching. A page whose plane itself is the point is `media.full`.

slots.name: media
slots.rationale: THE SLOT GIVES THE WIDTH. The plane renders faithfully inside it at equal unit scale and its height follows from the authored domain. FIT: fill — the slot width IS the media's width and the authored domain decides the height. There is no height cap and the page scrolls.

slots.name: interpretation
slots.rationale: The reading OF the visual. Mayer's spatial-contiguity principle is why it is in this pattern at all rather than further down a generic page.

slots.rationale: What the visual establishes, stated once.

visual.explanation.readingMeasure: interpretation is 466px in `side` and 760px in `stacked` — both inside the measure, and both a grid position rather than a chosen number.
visual.explanation.mediaSlotBehaviour: THE SLOT DECIDES THE WIDTH; THE AUTHORED DOMAIN DECIDES THE HEIGHT. Four approved desktop spans — 6, 7, 8 and 12 columns — and the renderer may not invent a fifth. The aspect class selects the family and span promotion selects among spans that clear the media's minimum legible width. There is no height ceiling: if a six-column slot makes a tall plane 950px high, the page scrolls.
visual.explanation.adversarialContent: A four-sentence interpretation against a nine-paragraph one, at both aspects — the prescribed subdesign and every slot width must be identical.
visual.explanation.residueRisk: A SIDE-BY-SIDE SUBDESIGN WAS DESIGNED, RENDERED, MEASURED AND REMOVED. Seven columns of plane beside five of reading fills the surface exactly and looks right when the reading runs to four paragraphs; with a one-sentence reading it left roughly 600px of empty column — the same rail this project has now rejected three times. A composition whose soundness depends on HOW MUCH PROSE THE AUTHOR HAPPENED TO WRITE is content-dependent, and content is exactly what may never decide a composition. So every visual pattern in this catalogue stacks its media and its reading, and the aspect class chooses only how wide the plane is.
visual.explanation.promotionOrder: Within one (surface, aspect class) the approved subdesigns are ordered by media span ascending and the FIRST whose span clears the media's minimum legible width is taken. balanced: 6 -> 8 -> 12 · landscape: 7 -> 8 -> 12 · portrait: 8 -> 12 · wide: 12.

Six columns of plane beside six of reading was rejected by measurement: a 717px portrait plane left 734px of nothing under the reading column — a plane no wider than it is tall cannot share a row with prose, in any composition. interactive.primary.intent: A manipulable object is the page: an opening brief, the instrument, and prompts directing what to try.

slots.name: intro
slots.rationale: What the object is and what changing it does. Read once, before touching anything.

slots.name: instrument
slots.rationale: The object and its controls as ONE slot: a control detached from what it controls is the spatial-contiguity failure in its purest form. NAMED `instrument`, not `workspace`: the practice patterns use `workspace` for the surface a learner writes ON, and one slot name carrying two slot types is the collision that attacks the two-vocabulary distinction directly.

slots.name: prompts
slots.rationale: What to try. Beside the instrument on desktop so the learner reads and acts without leaving either.

slots.name: synthesis
slots.rationale: What the exploration was for.

practice.workbook.intent: A question set beside a workspace the learner acts on — lined paper or grid paper — with the stimulus staying while the worklist moves.

slots.name: intro
slots.rationale: What this set is for, and the convention to work to.

slots.name: reference
slots.rationale: A worked plane to plot against, when the task is to reproduce or extend one. Above the questions in the same column, so the workspace beside them spans both rows — putting it in a row BELOW left a 600px dead column whenever the plotting surface was tall. FIT: fill — the slot width IS the media's width and the authored domain decides the height. There is no height cap and the page scrolls.

slots.name: questions
slots.rationale: THE ONE SLOT IN THE CATALOGUE THAT OWNS A LOCAL VERTICAL SCROLL, and only because the workspace beside it must stay put. A template feature, never a way of making teaching content shorter.

slots.name: workspace
slots.rationale: Where the learner writes or plots. THE SHEET IS A WINDOW AND THE PAPER SCROLLS INSIDE IT — more paper never means smaller writing. LINED VERSUS GRID PAPER IS A PROPERTY OF THE BLOCK, not of this slot and not of the pattern: the catalogue previously forked into two patterns over it, which is a pattern forking on a block property.
